source_text: {ΠΑΛΛ.} Σαφὴς μὲν εὖ μάλα, πλὴν ἀποχρῶν ἥκιστά γε. {ΚΥΡ.} Βούλει δὴ οὖν ἐπ' ἐκεῖνο πάλιν προθυμότατα διαστείχωμεν, ὃ τοῖς ἐπ' αὐτῇ διηγήμασιν ἐλλελοιπέναι δοκεῖ; οἴει γάρ που, κατὰ τὸ εἰκὸς, προσεπάγεσθαι δεῖν τὸν σαφηνιοῦντα λόγον, τίνα μὲν ἡμῖν ἐγήγερται τρόπον, πηνίκα δὲ καὶ ὅπως τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συντέθειται δικαιώματά τε καὶ νόμοι, καὶ ἐγκαινισμὸς καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ κρίσις. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Φράζε δὴ οὖν τὰ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ πάλιν· διανοῇ γὰρ ὀρθῶς. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐρῶ μὲν ἐγώ. Σὺ δὲ αὖ συγγνώμων ἔσο, τὴν εἰσάπαν δυσχέρειαν τῶν θεωρημάτων ἐννενοηκὼς, κἂν εἴπου τι λέγοιμι τυχὸν τῶν ἀκριβείας ἡμαρτηκότων, καὶ λόγου τοῦ δέοντος ἐκπεφοιτηκότων, μετάπλαττε καὶ μεθάρμοζε. Συλλήπτορα γάρ σε καὶ ἀρωγὸν τῶν ἐμαυτοῦ ποιήσομαι λόγων. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἴθι Θεῷ πίσυνος. {ΚΥΡ.} Συμπεπερασμένων δὴ οὖν εὖ μάλα τῶν ἔργων τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἑκάστου τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ σοφῶς καὶ εὐτέχνως ἐκπεποιημένων πρός γε τὸ παραδειχθὲν ἐν τῷ ὄρει κάλλος, ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων, «Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ μηνὸς τοῦ πρώτου, νεομηνίᾳ, στήσεις τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου.» Καὶ μεθ' ἕτερα πάλιν· «Καὶ ἐγένετο, φησὶν, ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τῷ πρώτῳ, τῷ δευτέρῳ ἔτει ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐξ Αἰγύπτου νεομηνίας, ἐστάθη ἡ σκηνὴ, καὶ ἔστησε Μωσῆς τὴν σκηνήν.» Ἐγήγερται μὲν οὖν, κατὰ τὸ Θεῷ δοκοῦν, ἡ ἀρχαία σκηνὴ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ νοουμένης Ἐκκλησίας, ἐφ' ἑαυτῇ τοὺς τύπους εὖ μάλα προσαναφαίνουσα. Πολυπραγμονῶμεν δὲ, εἰ δοκεῖ, τὰς αἰτίας τοῦ διὰ Μωσέως ἐγηγέρθαι μᾶλλον αὐτὴν, σεσιγημένου πρὸς τὸ παρὸν Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναυῆ, καίτοι παρεστηκότος ἀεὶ τῷ παναρίστῳ Μωσῇ, καὶ συναναθρώσκοντος μὲν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος τὸ Σινᾶ, πολεμοῦντος δὲ καὶ ἀντεξάγοντος τῷ Ἀμαλὴκ διὰ φωνῆς Μωσέως. Ἔφη γάρ που πρὸς αὐτὸν, «Ἐπίλεξαι σεαυτῷ ἄνδρας δυνατοὺς, καὶ ἐξελθὼν παράταξαι τῷ Ἀμαλὴκ αὔριον.» Καὶ παρετάξατο, καὶ νενίκηκε. Τίς οὖν ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ τοῦδε λόγος, οὐ δοκιμάζειν ἄξιον; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν δρωμένων τὸν τοῦ μυστηρίου λόγον εἴπερ ἕλοιτό τις ἐξακριβοῦν ὡς ἔνι, κατατεθηπὼς ἐρεῖ τὸ, «Ὦ βάθος πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως Θεοῦ!» Ἄθρει γὰρ ὅπως λεπτός τε καὶ ἀναγκαῖος ὁ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ νοῦς· ἀναθέοντι μὲν γὰρ εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῷ θεσπεσίῳ Μωσῇ, συνάνεισιν Ἰησοῦς· οὐ γὰρ προσιτὸς ἑτέρως ὁ Πατὴρ, εἰ μὴ δι' Υἱοῦ. Καὶ γάρ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς, εἰ λέγοιτο· «Οὐδεὶς ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα, εἰ μὴ δι' ἐμοῦ.» Ἐν Χριστῷ τοιγαροῦν καὶ αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἁγίοις ἡ πρόσοδος· καὶ οὐκ ἄν τις δύναιτο, καθάπερ εἰς ὄρος, ἀναπηδᾷν εἰς ὑψηλήν τινα καὶ ὑπερφερῆ θεωρίαν, ἀλλ' οὐδ' ἂν, οἶμαι, τὶς ἀγχοῦ γένοιτο Θεοῦ, κατὰ τρόπον δὲ δηλονότι συν
pass_a_gloss: Pall.: Clear (σαφής) very much, but sufficient (ἀποχρῶν) least of all. Cyr.: Do you wish that we go through again most eagerly to that which seems to have been left out (ἐλλελοιπέναι) in the narratives (διηγήματα) about it? For you think, as is likely, that one must add the clarifying account: in what way it was raised (ἐγήγερται) for us, and when and how the things in it were composed (συντέθειται): ordinances (δικαιώματα) and laws (νόμοι), and dedication (ἐγκαινισμός) and sanctification (ἁγιασμός) and judgment (κρίσις). Pall.: Tell (φράζε) the things on each again; for you think rightly (ὀρθῶς). Cyr.: Then I will speak. You be forgiving (συγγνώμων), having considered the entire difficulty (δυσχέρεια) of the contemplations (θεωρήματα); and if anywhere I say something that has missed exactness (ἀκρίβεια) and wandered off (ἐκπεφοιτηκότων) from the needed account, reshape (μετάπλαττε) and readjust (μεθάρμοζε). For I will make you co-helper (συλλήπτωρ) and aid (ἀρωγός) of my words. Pall.: Go, trusting God (Θεῷ πίσυνος). Cyr.: The works of the holy tent having been completed well, and each of the things in it wisely and skilfully made toward the beauty shown (παραδειχθέν) on the mountain, the Lord spoke to Moses: 'On day one (ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ) of the first month, at new moon (νεομηνίᾳ), you will set up (στήσεις) the tent of witness (μαρτυρίου).' And after other things: 'And it happened in the first month, in the second year of their going out from Egypt, at new moon, the tent was set up, and Moses set up the tent.' So the ancient tent of the Church understood in Christ was raised according to God's will, showing forth beforehand (προσαναφαίνουσα) the types (τύποι) on itself. Let us investigate (πολυπραγμονῶμεν) the causes of its being raised rather through Moses, Joshua (Ἰησοῦς) son of Nun being kept silent for the present, though always standing beside (παρεστηκότος) the all-excellent Moses, and going up together onto Mount Sinai, and warring and marching out against Amalek through Moses' voice. For he said to him: 'Choose for yourself mighty men, and going out draw up (παράταξαι) against Amalek tomorrow.' And he drew up and has conquered (νενίκηκε). What then is the reason (λόγος) of this; is it not worth testing (δοκιμάζειν)? Pall.: Very much so. Cyr.: If someone should choose to examine exactly the reason of the mystery (μυστήριον) in each of the things done, astonished he will say: 'O depth of riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!' Look how subtle (λεπτός) and necessary (ἀναγκαῖος) the sense (νοῦς) in each: to the godlike (θεσπέσιος) Moses running up into the mountain Joshua goes up together; for the Father is not otherwise approachable (προσιτός) except through Son. For it is true if it be said: 'No one comes to the Father except through me.' In Christ therefore also for the saints themselves is the approach (πρόσοδος); and no one could leap up (ἀναπηδᾶν), as into a mountain, into some high and surpassing contemplation (θεωρία), nor, I think, would anyone come near (ἀγχοῦ) God, in the manner (κατὰ τρόπον) clearly of con-[junction, continued in §3].
pass_b_english: Palladius: Very clear indeed, but far from enough.

Cyril: Then would you like us to go back with all eagerness to the point that seems to have been left out of what we said about it? For you think, I suppose, and naturally so, that we must add an account that makes clear how it was set up for us, and when and how the ordinances and laws connected with it were established, together with its dedication, its sanctification and its judgment.
Palladius: Then explain each of these in turn, for you are thinking rightly.

Cyril: I will speak, then. But you in turn must be indulgent, bearing in mind how altogether difficult these contemplations are. If at any point I happen to say something that misses precision and strays from what ought to be said, reshape it and set it right; for I will make you a partner and helper in my words.
Palladius: Go on, trusting in God.

Cyril: When the work on the holy tent had been fully completed, and each of the things in it had been made with wisdom and skill after the beauty shown on the mountain (Exodus 25:40), the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: ‘On one day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall set up the tent of witness’ (Exodus 40:2). And again, further on: ‘And it came to pass,’ it says, ‘in the first month, in the second year after they went out of Egypt, at the new moon, that the tent was set up, and Moses set up the tent’ (Exodus 40:17–18). So the ancient tent was set up as God willed. It was the tent of the Church that is understood in Christ, and it showed beforehand in itself, very clearly, the types of that Church. Let us inquire closely, if you agree, why it was set up by Moses rather than by another, while Joshua the son of Nun is passed over in silence for the present. Yet Joshua always stood beside the most excellent Moses (Exodus 24:13); he went up with him onto Mount Sinai, and he made war and marched out against Amalek at Moses’ word. For Moses said to him: ‘Choose for yourself mighty men, and go out and draw up for battle against Amalek tomorrow’ (Exodus 17:9). And he drew up for battle, and he won (Exodus 17:10–13). What, then, is the reason for this? Is it not worth examining?

Cyril: If anyone chooses to work out, as exactly as he can, the meaning of the mystery in each of these events, he will say in amazement: ‘O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!’ (Romans 11:33). See how subtle and how necessary the sense of each detail is. When the inspired Moses goes up the mountain, Joshua goes up with him; for the Father cannot be approached in any other way than through the Son. Indeed, the saying is true: ‘No one comes to the Father except through me’ (John 14:6). So even for the saints themselves the approach is in Christ. anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Exodus 40:2 LXX reads 'Ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ' (a Hebraism for 'on the first day'); rendered 'On one day' because Cyril's exegesis in §§3-4 turns on 'one day'. Exodus 40:17-18: Cyril's quotation runs from verse 17 into the first clause of verse 18. 'The beauty shown on the mountain' alludes to Exodus 25:40 (LXX 'τὸν τύπον τὸν δεδειγμένον σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει'); cf. Exodus 25:9. 'Always stood beside' echoes Exodus 24:13 LXX 'Ἰησοῦς ὁ παρεστηκὼς αὐτῷ', which also records Joshua going up the mountain with Moses. Exodus 17:9 LXX has 'Ἐπίλεξον'; Cyril's 'Ἐπίλεξαι' is a middle form, same sense. Joshua is 'Ἰησοῦς' in Greek, the same name as Jesus; Cyril's typology (Joshua goes up with Moses as the Son leads to the Father) depends on this, but the English follows Book 3 and says 'Joshua'. 'δικαιώματα' may echo Hebrews 9:1 ('δικαιώματα λατρείας'); not cited. 'κρίσις' (judgment) left plain; it may point to the 'oracle of judgment' (Exodus 28:15, 28:30), not cited. The section ends mid-word (συν|αφείας); the English breaks at 'by way of' and resumes in §3 with 'union'.

changes: μεθ' ἕτερα: 'a little later' -> 'further on' (Exodus 40:17 is 15 verses on)
'a tabernacle of the Church' -> 'the tabernacle' (Greek has the article)
added 'rather than by another' for μᾶλλον
archaic 'if it be said' -> 'the saying is true'
κατὰ τρόπον συναφείας: removed doubled 'in the proper manner, that is'; now 'by way of union'
